problem.text: Call a set of integers "spacy" if it contains no more than one out of any three consecutive integers. How many subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 12\}$, including the empty set, are spacy?

steps.title: Where to start: count for smaller sets first
steps.body: The spacy rule only looks at numbers that are close together, so the question for $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ should depend on the answers for a slightly shorter list. Let $a_n$ be the number of spacy subsets of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, including the empty set. Start with the smallest cases.

your_turn.answer: $a_1 = 2$, $a_2 = 3$, $a_3 = 4$. With $n \le 3$ all the numbers lie in one block of three consecutive integers, so a spacy subset is empty or has one element.

steps.title: Split on whether $n$ is in the subset
steps.body:
If the subset does not contain $n$, it is just a spacy subset of $\{1, \ldots, n-1\}$: that gives $a_{n-1}$ subsets. If it does contain $n$, then $n-1$ and $n-2$ must be left out, and the rest is any spacy subset of $\{1, \ldots, n-3\}$: that gives $a_{n-3}$ subsets. So
$$a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-3}$$

your_turn.prompt: In the case where $n$ is in the subset, why is every spacy subset of $\{1, \ldots, n-3\}$ allowed for the rest?
your_turn.answer: The only block of three consecutive numbers in $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ that contains $n$ is $n-2, n-1, n$, and $n-1$, $n-2$ are left out. Every other block lies inside $\{1, \ldots, n-1\}$, where only numbers up to $n-3$ can be chosen, and those form a spacy set.

steps.title: Check the rule and build up
steps.body: The rule gives $a_4 = a_3 + a_1 = 4 + 2 = 6$. Check by listing: the empty set, $\{1\}$, $\{2\}$, $\{3\}$, $\{4\}$ and $\{1, 4\}$. Careful: the step back is to $a_{n-3}$ (three places back), not $a_{n-2}$.
